solutionsIndex.title: Outbound work, run as an operation rather than an experiment
solutionsIndex.lead: Four services that share one method. Pick the one that matches the job you need done, or tell us the outcome and we will say which of them gets you there.

appointmentSetting.body: Meetings booked into the calendar of whoever will run them, against criteria you write down before we start.

outboundSales.body: A trained team selling on your behalf, from your script, your pricing and your compliance rules.

customerService.body: Inbound calls, follow-ups and overflow answered in the customer language, without new headcount.

leadGeneration.body: Lists built, contacts verified and first touch made, so your pipeline starts with people who actually answer.

engagement.title: Three ways to run this
engagement.lead: The right shape depends on how certain you are that outbound works for what you sell. Most companies start in the middle.

models.title: Pilot
models.body: A fixed period at agreed volume, priced as a project. You find out what the market says before committing to a team.

models.title: Dedicated team
models.body: A named group working only on your campaigns, at a monthly rate. The usual choice once a pilot has proved out.

models.title: Overflow
models.body: We take the calls your own team cannot reach in time. Sized by hours rather than headcount, and it flexes with your season.

shared.noFitNote: If you recognise yourself on this list, say so on the first call. Turning down work that will not perform is cheaper for both of us than proving it over three months.

appointmentSetting.title: Meetings your sales team is glad to have in the calendar
appointmentSetting.lead: The hard part of appointment setting is not booking meetings. It is booking the ones that are worth the travel time. We agree the criteria in writing first, and a meeting only counts when it meets them.
appointmentSetting.capabilitiesLead: Every step is set up so the person who runs the meeting knows exactly what was promised on the call.

capabilities.title: Criteria before calls
capabilities.body: Company size, role, budget signal, timing. Written down and agreed before the first dial, so nobody argues about what counts afterwards.

capabilities.title: Research per account
capabilities.body: The caller knows what the company does before dialling. Generic openers are the fastest way to get hung up on.

capabilities.title: Direct calendar booking
capabilities.body: We book into the calendar of the person running the meeting, with the notes attached, so nothing is retyped or lost in a handover.

capabilities.title: Confirmation and reminder
capabilities.body: Every booking is confirmed in writing and reminded before the day. It is the single cheapest way to cut no-shows.

capabilities.title: No-show recovery
capabilities.body: A missed meeting is followed up and rebooked rather than written off. Most of them were a diary problem, not a rejection.

appointmentSetting.deliverablesLead: You should never have to ask how the campaign is going. It should already be in front of you.

deliverables.title: Meetings in the calendar
deliverables.body: With the account research, the objection raised and what was actually promised on the call attached to the invitation.

deliverables.title: Weekly report
deliverables.body: Dials, conversations, bookings, no-shows and the objections we heard most. One page, same format every week.

deliverables.title: Call recordings
deliverables.body: All of them, not a highlight reel. Listen to any conversation made in your name.

deliverables.title: Market feedback
deliverables.body: What the market said about your price, your positioning and your competitors. Often worth more than the meetings.

fit: You sell to businesses and the deal needs a conversation
Your sellers are good in the room but slow to fill it
The customer value justifies a meeting that costs real time
You can take meetings within two to three weeks of booking
noFit: You need consumer volume rather than business meetings
The product only makes sense after a long technical demo we cannot give
Nobody on your side has time to actually attend the meetings
The offer has not been sold successfully by anyone yet, including you

faq.q: What counts as a booked meeting?
faq.a: Whatever we write down together before the campaign starts. Usually a decision maker at a company of a given size who has confirmed a time and knows what the meeting is about. If it does not meet the criteria, it does not go on the invoice.

faq.q: Do you use our name or yours?
faq.a: Yours. We call as an extension of your company, with your email signature and your phone presentation. That is also why every call is recorded and available to you.

faq.q: How many meetings can we expect?
faq.a: We will not give you a number before we have heard your offer and seen your list, because any figure quoted at that stage is guesswork. After a pilot we can tell you what your market actually gives, and that number is worth something.

faq.q: Who provides the list?
faq.a: Either side. If you have a CRM full of dormant accounts that is usually the best place to start. If not, we build and clean a list as part of the setup.

faq.q: What happens with no-shows?
faq.a: They are followed up and rebooked. Under the standard agreement a meeting that never happens and cannot be rebooked is credited, because you should not pay for an empty calendar slot.

outboundSales.title: A sales floor you do not have to build yourself
outboundSales.lead: Hiring, training and managing outbound sellers is a business in itself. We already run one. You get the output of a trained team without the eighteen months it takes to get one working.
outboundSales.capabilitiesLead: The team works to your rules. What we bring is the discipline that makes a phone floor produce consistently.

capabilities.title: Your script, our delivery
capabilities.body: You own the offer and the pricing. We turn it into something that survives contact with a sceptical person on the third call of their morning.

capabilities.title: Objection library
capabilities.body: Every objection heard is logged and answered, and the answer goes to the whole floor. The team gets better weekly rather than individually.

capabilities.title: Compliance built in
capabilities.body: Consent recorded on the call where the rules require it, opt-outs honoured immediately, and no pressure tactics. A sale that gets cancelled costs everyone.

capabilities.title: Order handling
capabilities.body: Orders land in your system in the format you use, with the recording reference attached to each one.

capabilities.title: Quality review
capabilities.body: Calls are sampled and scored by a team lead, not only by the numbers. Volume without quality is just churn arriving later.

outboundSales.deliverablesLead: Sales, and the evidence behind each one.

deliverables.title: Closed sales
deliverables.body: In your system, in your format, with the call recording reference on every order.

deliverables.title: Weekly performance report
deliverables.body: Conversion by list segment and by seller, so you can see where the offer works rather than only whether it works.

deliverables.title: Objection and price feedback
deliverables.body: What the market says about your pricing, in volume. This is the part that changes your positioning.

deliverables.title: Recordings and consent trail
deliverables.body: Retrievable per order, which is what makes a disputed sale a two-minute conversation instead of a problem.

fit: The product can be explained and closed inside one call
Pricing is clear enough that a trained caller can quote it
You want volume that your own team cannot generate
You are ready to act on what the market tells you about your offer
noFit: The sale needs a technical specialist on the line
Pricing is negotiated individually on every deal
You expect us to sell something you would not buy yourself
The margin cannot carry the cost of a call that does not close

faq.q: Do you work on commission only?
faq.a: No. Commission-only outbound sounds attractive and reliably produces the wrong behaviour on the phone, because the incentive is to close anything rather than the right thing. We price on a monthly rate, usually with a performance component on top.

faq.q: How long before we see results?
faq.a: First conversations in week one. A usable read on conversion after three to four weeks, because that is roughly when there is enough volume to tell a real pattern from a good week.

faq.q: Who is legally responsible for the sale?
faq.a: You are the seller and the contract is with you. We are your processor: we make the call, record the consent and hand the order over. The data processing agreement sets this out before the campaign starts.

faq.q: Can you sell to consumers?
faq.a: We take consumer campaigns only where the rules are clearly satisfied, which in Denmark means the Robinson list and the consent requirements in the marketing act. If a campaign cannot be run cleanly we say no.

faq.q: What if the campaign is not working?
faq.a: You will know by the second weekly report, and we will tell you before you have to ask. Then we either change the offer, change the list, or stop. The agreement is monthly precisely so that stopping is a normal option.

customerService.title: Someone answers, in the language the customer called in
customerService.lead: An unanswered call is a cancelled customer that has not filled in the form yet. We take the calls you cannot get to, in the language they came in, without adding a single person to your payroll.
customerService.capabilitiesLead: Set up as an extension of your own service, not as a wall in front of it.

capabilities.title: Overflow or full line
capabilities.body: Take everything, or only what your own team cannot reach within your target. Both are normal, and you can move between them.

capabilities.title: Your systems
capabilities.body: The team works in your helpdesk and your phone system, so history stays in one place and nothing has to be synced afterwards.

capabilities.title: Escalation rules
capabilities.body: We agree exactly what we resolve and what goes to you, in writing. Ambiguity here is what makes outsourced service feel like a maze.

capabilities.title: Danish and English
capabilities.body: Both answered by someone who actually speaks them, so an English-speaking customer does not land in a Danish queue.

capabilities.title: Saves and retention
capabilities.body: A cancellation call handled well is often a customer kept. Those conversations get the experienced people on the floor.

customerService.deliverablesLead: Coverage, plus a clear view of what your customers are actually calling about.

deliverables.title: Answered calls
deliverables.body: Logged in your system with notes, so your own team picks up mid-thread without asking the customer to repeat themselves.

deliverables.title: Weekly service report
deliverables.body: Volume, answer time, resolution rate and the reasons people called, grouped so the pattern is visible.

deliverables.title: Recurring-issue list
deliverables.body: The top reasons for contact each month. This is where you find the product fix that removes a hundred calls.

deliverables.title: Recordings
deliverables.body: Available for training and for any disputed conversation.

fit: You lose calls at peaks, in the evening or during holidays
You get calls in English but staff only for Danish
Your team is answering the same question all day
Answer time is hurting your reviews or your churn
noFit: Every case needs deep product access we cannot be given
Regulation requires your own certified staff on the line
Volume is so low that a shared line would cost more than it saves
Nobody on your side can own the escalation rules

faq.q: Do you use our own systems?
faq.a: Yes. We work in your helpdesk and your telephony under named user accounts, so history stays in one place and access can be withdrawn instantly if the arrangement ends.

faq.q: Will customers know they are talking to an agency?
faq.a: Not unless you want them to. We answer in your name, with your greeting. If a customer asks directly, we do not lie about it.

faq.q: What are your opening hours?
faq.a: We set them per campaign to match where your customers are and when they call. Extended hours cost more, so it is worth checking your traffic pattern before buying evenings you do not need.

faq.q: How do you handle a customer who wants to cancel?
faq.a: By the rules you set. If retention is in scope, the experienced people take those calls and the outcome is reported separately, so you can see what the saves are actually worth.

faq.q: Can you handle email and chat too?
faq.a: Email and ticket follow-up, yes. Live chat is available in the larger setups, where volume justifies a dedicated seat.

leadGeneration.title: A pipeline that starts with contacts who exist
leadGeneration.lead: Most outbound underperforms for an unglamorous reason: the list is wrong. Dead numbers, people who left two years ago, companies in the wrong segment. We fix the list before anyone spends a day dialling it.
leadGeneration.capabilitiesLead: Unglamorous work that decides whether everything downstream is worth doing.

capabilities.title: Segment definition
capabilities.body: We agree what a target account looks like in terms you can check: size, sector, geography, and the signal that makes them worth a call now.

capabilities.title: List building
capabilities.body: Built from public registers and your own data rather than bought as a bulk file of unknown age.

capabilities.title: Data cleaning
capabilities.body: Dead numbers removed, roles verified, duplicates merged against your CRM so your own sellers are not calling in parallel.

capabilities.title: First-touch qualification
capabilities.body: A short call that establishes whether there is a reason to talk further, without trying to force a meeting that is not there.

capabilities.title: Opt-out handling
capabilities.body: Anyone who says no is suppressed permanently across every campaign we run for you. It is a legal requirement and a reputational one.

leadGeneration.deliverablesLead: A list you can hand to a seller without apologising for it.

deliverables.title: Verified contact list
deliverables.body: In your CRM format, with the source and verification date on every record.

deliverables.title: Qualified leads
deliverables.body: Contacts who confirmed a relevant need, with the notes from the conversation attached.

deliverables.title: Suppression list
deliverables.body: Everyone who opted out, so nobody in your organisation calls them again by accident.

deliverables.title: Segment read
deliverables.body: Which parts of the segment responded and which were dead. This is what tells you where to aim next quarter.

fit: Your CRM is full of records nobody trusts
You are entering a market and have no list at all
Your sellers spend more time researching than selling
You want to test a segment before committing a team to it
noFit: You want a bulk file cheaply and do not care about accuracy
The target group cannot be identified from public data
You have no capacity to follow up the leads once they land
The plan depends on contacting people who have already opted out

faq.q: Where does the data come from?
faq.a: Public company registers, your own CRM, and verification by phone. We do not buy anonymous bulk files, because there is no way to document where the data came from, and that is exactly what you need if anyone asks.

faq.q: Is this GDPR compliant?
faq.a: B2B contact data for a relevant business purpose is normally handled under legitimate interest, with a documented assessment and a working opt-out. We sign a data processing agreement before any data changes hands.

faq.q: Do we own the list afterwards?
faq.a: Yes. The list is yours, delivered in your format, and it stays yours if the arrangement ends. We keep no copy beyond the retention period in the agreement.

faq.q: How current is the data?
faq.a: Every record carries its verification date. Contact data decays at roughly two to three percent a month, which is why a list is a living thing rather than a one-off purchase.

faq.q: Can you enrich our existing CRM instead?
faq.a: Often the better place to start. Dormant accounts that already know your name convert considerably better than cold ones, and the cleaning work is cheaper than building from nothing.
